The present anticipatory bail application has been filed by the applicant - Piyush Kohli seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.07 of 2020, under Sections 354, 354Kha, 323, 506, 376 I.P.C.,
Police Station Mahila Thana, District Moradabad.

3. The FIR of the present matter was lodged on 16.01.2020 for offences under Sections 354,
354-Kha, 323, 506 I.P.C. by the victim against the applicant, Vijay Mehta and Piyush Kohli on the basis of an application addressed to the Senior Superintendent of Police, Moradabad with the allegation that she was previously working in Hydo Design Management Company, Noida.

sentences.text: On 14.12.2019 in the afternoon she received a phone call from Sudhir Gupta the owner of the company on which he stated that if she again wants the work in the company then she may meet him near the petrol pump Peeli Kothi, Moradabad where he has come for some work.
He will increase her salary also.

She being unemployed and taking the words of Sudhir Gupta correct reached the said place at about 09:30 pm where she met the accused persons who told her to sit in the car and were talking to her and assured her that her job is confirmed and she may eat sweets due to the said reason.
She then consumed the sweets given to her by Sudhir Gupta after which she became intoxicated.
The accused persons then took her to a lonely place and forcibly enraged her modesty and tried to force upon her.
They tore her clothes and assaulted her.
On her raising a shout, they assaulted her and while going threatened her of not disclosing it to anyone.
She then came to understand that they had come there in a planned manner.
On 15.12.2019 she went to the Mahila Thana, Moradabad for lodging a report and gives an application but no action was taken.
She has then come with an application for lodging of her report and appropriate legal action.

Per Contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail vehemently and submitted as under :-

(i) The order sheet of the trial court which is annexed as S.A-1 to the supplementary affidavit dated 01.09.2024, from 23.03.2023 to 23.08.2024 shows that non-bailable warrants have been issued against the applicant.

(ii) Since the applicant has been summoned by the court concerned and he has failed to appear before it, non-bailable warrants issued against him and as such he has been avoiding the process of law and absconding and as such in view of the judgements of Apex Court in the case of State of Haryana vs. Dharamraj : 2023 SCC OnLine SC 1085 and in the case of Srikant Upadhyay vs. State of Bihar : 2024 SCC Online SC 282 the applicant is not entitled for grant of anticipatory bail.

"It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may very graciously be pleased to allow this application and grant the Anticipatory Bail to the applicant during the pendency of his trial in FIR/Case Crime No. 07 of 2020, under Section 354, 354-Kha, 323, 506, 376 I.P.C., Police Station Mahila Thana, District Moradabad.

She being unemployed and taking the words of Sudhir Gupta correct reached the said place at about 09:30 pm where she met the accused persons who told her to sit in the car and were talking to her and assured her that her job is confirmed and she may eat sweets due to the said reason.

i) The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
This incident is of 14.12.2019 at about 09:30 pm but the FIR has been lodged after one month and two days on 16.01.2020.

The informant then filed an objection/protest petition dated 15.10.2020 supported by her affidavit which was directed to be treated as a complaint.

After rejection of the final report No. 16/2020 dated 03.08.2020 the matter was directed to be treated as a complaint and be listed for recording of the statement of the complainant under Section 200 Cr.P.C. vide order dated 09.12.2020.

sentences.text: After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records along with the dictum of the Apex Court, it is apparent that the applicant is named in the FIR.
He is the owner of a company.
The victim was an employee in the said company.
The identity of the applicant cannot be disputed as he was the employer of the victim/first informant.
Bailable warrants have been issued against the applicant after his non appearance to the call through summoning order.
The medical evidence does not rule out sexual violence on the victim.
The applicant has been summoned by an order of the court of competent jurisdiction.
I do not find it a fit case for interference.
11. Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application is rejected."

7. Against the said order, a Special Leave Petition was preferred before the Apex Court in which on 15.05.2024, notice was issued and the non-bailable warrant was converted to bailable warrant and the petitioner therein was directed to appear before the trial court and furnish bail.

The said order reads as under :-
"ORDER 1. Delay condoned.
2. We have heard Mr. D.P. Singh, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner.
3. Issue notice, returnable on 22 July, 2024.
4. In the facts and circumstances of the case we deem fit to convert the non-bailable warrant issued against the petitioner to a bailable warrant of the like amount.
We direct the petitioner to appear before the trial court and furnish the bail."
8. Subsequently, the said Special Leave Petition was disposed of vide order dated 22.07.2024 by which the interim order was made absolute and the petition was disposed of.

The said order reads as under :-
"ORDER Delay condoned in re-filing is condoned.

This Court had allowed interim protection to the petitioner on 15th May, 2024 consequent to which petitioner has appeared before the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 1, Moradabad and furnished bail.

Insofar as, the variation in the version of the victim is concerned, the Apex Court in the case of "X" vs. State of Maharastra (Supra) has held that the same cannot be considered while granting the anticipatory bail.
10. The applicant is named in the F.I.R. and there are allegations against him therein and also in the statements of victim recorded during investigation and further in the protest petition.
The applicant has been summoned by the court concerned and is absconding and avoiding the process of law.
No ground for interference is made out in the anticipatory bail application.
11. Accordingly, the present anticipatory bail is rejected.
